They materialized the full [.,4096,64,64] rel_h/rel_w for the global blocks before adding; ttnn.add broadcasts [.,g,1]+[.,1,g]->[.,g,g] NATIVELY (probed PCC 0.9999974), so the repeats were pure overhead. No fusion -- just redundant-op deletion.
sam_relpos_redundant_op_removal.measured_tracy: vision-prefill DEVICE time 587.9ms -> 423.8ms (-28%, 1.39x); Repeat op 202.9ms -> 0.00ms (net -164ms: BinaryNg rose 100.7->137.9ms as the broadcast folds into the add). Per-op after: BinaryNg 32.5%, Matmul 28.2%, Reshape 23.5%.
sam_relpos_redundant_op_removal.correctness: SAM encoder 0.99937 + DeepEncoder 0.99661 = BIT-IDENTICAL to before removal; structure 0; bf8 intact (16 call sites).
sam_relpos_redundant_op_removal.remaining_TM: Reshape (23.5%) + the risen BinaryNg -> addressed by the rel-pos TILE-add fusion below.

sam_relpos_tile_add_fusion.verdict: Layout fusion: do the GLOBAL-block rel-pos broadcast-add in TILE layout instead of ROW_MAJOR (window blocks kept ROW_MAJOR -- g=14 not tile-aligned, TILE is slower there). Root finding: the ROW_MAJOR double-broadcast add was the real cost, not the reshapes (isolated micro-bench: global add RM 21.4ms vs TILE 4.5ms per layer). Math unchanged (bf16 tilize/untilize exact) -> PCC bit-identical.
sam_relpos_tile_add_fusion.measured_tracy: vision-prefill DEVICE time 423.8ms -> 370.3ms (-12.6%). BinaryNg 137.9->70.4ms (global add 85.5->18.0ms = 4x4.51ms TILE vs 4x21.37ms RM); +13.8ms new untilize-flatten +0.8ms tilize; Reshape ~unchanged (99.6->99.0ms). Cumulative prefill: 587.9ms(bf8) -> 423.8(repeat-removal) -> 370.3(TILE-add) = -37% total, all PCC bit-identical.
sam_relpos_tile_add_fusion.correctness: SAM encoder 0.99937, DeepEncoder 0.99661 = bit-identical; full suite green (0 failed/3 skipped); structure 0; 0 torch in forwards; bf8 intact.
sam_relpos_tile_add_fusion.inherent: window rel-pos add 35.7ms (g=14 non-tile-aligned, TILE slower); matmuls 119.7ms + SDPA 7.7ms (fidelity/op fixed); the [.,4096,4096] dense mask + final tilize (SDPA needs a dense TILE attn_mask; all-TILE reshape P2 measured 44.5ms far worse). These are the floor without changing numerics/op.

conv_stay_2d.goal: SAM convs stay fully on-device in 2D; eliminate the T3K-guarded TTNNReshape torch-fallback in the conv output path.
conv_stay_2d.how: reshape_output=False (returns native flattened [1,1,H*W,C], no TTNNReshape) + pre-recorded model_config[<conv>]['input_shapes'] so H,W is supplied when chained on flattened tensors; LayerNorm2d runs on the flattened channel-last form; the one 4D reshape (patch_embed -> windowed SAM blocks) uses a PURE on-device ttnn.reshape (P150-native), not the guarded wrapper. Additive to modeling_unlimited_ocr.py TTNNUnlimitedOcrSamEncoder (no shared-module edits).
conv_stay_2d.verified: fast micro-loop (~8-10s/conv, no model load): neck_conv1 0.999955, neck_conv2 0.999904, net_2 0.999813, net_3 0.999731 -- all fallback=False, output flattened [1,1,H*W,C]. Full-model: SAM encoder 0.99943, DeepEncoder 0.99640 (unchanged), 0 'running torch fallback' warnings in the whole run; Tier4 sam/deep tests pass (exit 0).
conv_stay_2d.bonus_done: vision prefill IS now trace-capturable (the conv fallback removal unblocked it). Added default-OFF enable_prefill_trace / demo --trace-prefill (@trace_enabled TTNNUnlimitedOcrPrefillGraph; independent prefill/decode trace scopes). GATES: TRACED-prefill==NORMAL 16/16 (adds zero error vs NORMAL's own bf16 divergence); new Tier4 test_traced_prefill_matches_normal PASS; suite 42/42; decode still 17.2 tok/s; structure 0; 0 torch in forwards. PERF (honest): prefill ~10.9s NORMAL -> ~10.7s traced = ~1-2% -- the vision tower is COMPUTE-bound (not host-dispatch-bound like decode), so trace helps little; shipped OPT-IN, not default (contrast decode trace = dispatch-bound = 4.7x, kept default-on). trace_region_size=400MB when prefill-trace on.

data_parallel.deadlock_fix: Prior attempt hung: the DP TEST spawned a child subprocess opening the (4,1) mesh while the parent pytest held a device -> whole-cluster-lock deadlock. Fixed: DP test opens the (4,1) mesh IN-PROCESS (no subprocess, no nested opens).
data_parallel.framework_constraint: Opening a (4,1) mesh then a (1,1) in the SAME process corrupts ttnn global mesh state (a (1,1) tensor gets a multi-shard ConcatMeshToTensor composer -> to_torch 'MeshCoordinate out of bounds'). So the DP test is OPT-IN (TT_UNLIMITED_OCR_DP=1), skipped by default, so collecting it with the (1,1) suite never opens the mesh. Single-device suite stays green.

multi_image_trace_replay.verdict: WORKS across different images AT THE SAME SEQUENCE SHAPE. Verified: 3 distinct docs (invoice/purchase_order/memorandum) under --trace-prefill (prefill+decode both traced), one pipeline / one captured trace reused across all 3 -> 3 of 3 DISTINCT outputs, each torch-matched (7/8, 8/8, 7/8). Also decode-only trace across 4 images verified earlier.
multi_image_trace_replay.why: prefill/decode graphs take pixel_values/token_ids/cos/sin as POSITIONAL device tensors that TracedRun refreshes per replay -> each image's data flows through the same captured graph; no stale-buffer bug.
multi_image_trace_replay.constraint: trace replay is valid ONLY for the captured SHAPE. Same prompt + fixed 1024 global view (273 vision tokens) -> same prefill seq len -> valid for any such image (content varies, shape fixed). DIFFERENT prompt length or resolution/crop count -> different seq len -> captured trace invalid; would need per-shape re-capture or prompt-length bucketing (dots_ocr nearest_bucket style), NOT yet implemented. Demo fixes the global-1024 view + one prompt to stay in-shape.
multi_image_trace_replay.timing: each image prefill 10.7s [traced] + decode 2.7s, 17.3 tok/s decode.
